newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Hungary Postabank super board quits on law change.
newsitem.headline: Hungary Postabank super board quits on law change.

text.p: The 24-member supervisory board of Hungary's Postabank Rt, the country's second largest commercial bank, resigned as changes in the law limited the number of members to nine, the bank said on Wednesday.
Jozsef Koblencz, chairman of the supervisory board told Reuters that the board resigned to help the work of the annual shareholders meeting, to be held on Friday.
The resignation of the board had no connection with a deposit withdrawal wave which hit Postabank in February, Koblencz said.

"This has absolutely nothing to do with (the withdrawals)," he said, adding that the shareholders' meeting will elect a new supervisory board and also a board of directors as the mandate of the current board of directors expired.
The agenda of the shareholders' meeting also includes a decision on a capital increase.
Postabank commissioned SBC Warburg earlier this year to find investors to raise the capital of the bank.
According to earlier press information, some of the Hungarian shareholders showed interest in raising Postabank's 16.45 billion forints ($90.2 million) registered capital.
Postabank said that it posted an after-tax profit of 5.6 million forints in 1996 on a balance sheet total of 378.7 billion forints.
